summary:
MISSION: OUTPOST is a cooperative Mars survival game and astronaut training simulator. Players take on crew roles, explore a Mars habitat, complete tasks, and manage shared resources as the mission advances through Martian days, or Sols. Teamwork matters: players coordinate responsibilities, respond to simulated events, and work toward mission objectives.

The project combines an explorable habitat and survival scenarios with a NASA Science Terminal. The terminal presents NASA DONKI space-weather observations and Mars rover imagery from NASA’s Image and Video Library, with source attribution. Real NASA observations are kept separate from fictional game events and simulated resource values.

MISSION: OUTPOST makes ideas about Mars exploration and crewed missions approachable through interactive play. It encourages communication, systems thinking, and curiosity about space science, and could support classroom or informal learning. Built with JavaScript, React, Vite, and Phaser, it is a browser-based prototype; some multiplayer and end-to-end mission features still need further testing.
details:
MISSION: OUTPOST is a cooperative Mars survival game and astronaut training simulator. Players take on crew roles, explore a Mars habitat, complete role-based tasks, and manage shared life-support resources across a sequence of Martian days, or Sols. Simulated hazards and mission events challenge the crew to communicate and make decisions together.

The project combines gameplay with real space science. It displays NASA DONKI space-weather observations and Mars imagery from NASA’s Image and Video Library, with source information and clear labels. NASA observations are kept separate from fictional game events and simulated resource values: DONKI data is not presented as a measurement of radiation inside the habitat or as the cause of an in-game emergency.

The game is intended to make space science and the complexity of a crewed Mars mission approachable. By giving players different responsibilities and shared goals, it encourages teamwork, communication, systems thinking, and curiosity about Mars and space weather. It could support classroom activities or informal science learning.

The project is built with JavaScript, React, Vite, Phaser, and CSS. It uses NASA’s DONKI and Image and Video Library APIs. Firebase Realtime Database integration is included in the codebase, alongside a local mock mode for development. The current chat service synchronizes across browser tabs on the same device; remote chat and live Firebase behavior still depend on configuration and further verification. The project runs in a web browser and does not require specialized hardware.

Our creative approach is to pair a colourful, explorable Mars habitat with a science terminal and Sol-based training scenarios. Players can connect NASA observations to the broader mission context while seeing which information is real and which is part of the simulation.

The team considered beginner-friendly explanations, reliable source attribution, missing API data and keys, differences between real observations and simulated consequences, role balance, multiplayer synchronization, and recovery from disconnects. The project is a developing prototype; some multiplayer and end-to-end mission features still need live testing.
